compliance.emc: FCC Part 15, Subpart B, Class A; ICES-003, Class A; EN 55032, Class A; EN 55024; EN 55035; EN 62479; EN 50663; EN 300 386; EN 301 489; EN 303 413; BSMI; VCCI CISPR 32, Class A; MTCTE; KC KS C 9832, Class A; KS C 9835; Anatel

features.gnss: internal GNSS receiver supporting GPS/QZSS L1 C/A, GLONASS L1OF, BeiDou B1, SBAS L1 C/A (WAAS, EGNOS, MSAS, GAGAN) and Galileo E1B/C; RF sensitivity -166 dBm, and the GNSS port supplies up to 5 V DC at 150 mA to an active antenna
features.optics-qsfp-dd: 400GE QSFP-DD DAC, AOC and AEC only - the datasheet lists these six as Compatible FABRIC Cable Types, not as optics, because they carry the chassis fabric to an S9705-48D or S9725-64E rather than user traffic
features.optics-sfp-plus: the two 10G SFP+ management ports take the same 10GBASE SFP+ ER/LR/SR and 1GBASE SFP EX/LX/SX modules the datasheet lists for the service ports; it publishes no separate compatibility list for them
features.optics-sfp28: 25GBASE SFP28 ZR/ER/LR/SR; 10GBASE SFP+ ER/LR/SR; 1GBASE SFP EX/LX/SX (datasheet compatible transceiver list)
features.timing-cable: 50 ohm SMA coaxial with a 1/4-36UNS-2B connector for GNSS; 50 ohm SMB coaxial with a 10-32UNF-2A connector for 1PPS and 10MHz, each limited to 3 m; shielded RJ45 for ToD, limited to 3 m

management.console: RJ45 and micro-USB serial console, both lettered IOIOI on the faceplate, 115200 8N1 no flow control; the micro-USB side needs a Silicon Labs CP210x driver
management.service-port: 1x USB 3.0 Type-A, described by the guide as a maintenance port
management.timing: GNSS SMA input, 1PPS and 10MHz SMB input/output and a ToD input/output RJ45; SyncE and IEEE 1588v2 with the Default, G.8265.1, G.8275.1 and G.8275.2 profiles plus SMPTE ST 2059-2 (extra licence), T-GM, T-BC/OC and T-TC. NOS integration is required to activate any of it

performance.cluster-scale: standalone or clustered from 2.4 Tb/s up to 134 Tb/s, interoperating with the rest of the S9700 series through an S9705-48D or S9725-64E fabric

platform.oem-alias: DriveNets NCP-64X12C-S (Network Cloud Packet forwarder, 64x1/10GE + 12x100 + 6x400). NOT A UFISPACE CLAIM - no UfiSpace document mentions DriveNets. The mapping is internal analysis: the okf `drivenets-ddc` bundle's 'DriveNets NCF/NCP to white-box hardware map (shipping platforms)' matches the roadmap slide's NCP-64X12C-S (J2C 2.4T) to this chassis on published silicon and port configuration. Recorded so a search for either name finds this box; no DriveNets figure or artwork is transcribed anywhere in this file.

power.circuit-reserve: at least 1300 W reserved on each of two independent power circuits (HIG Installation Environment Requirements)
power.input-ac: 100 to 240 V, 12 A max per feed
power.input-dc: -40 to -75 V, 40 A max per feed

configs.description: Dual 1300 W AC supplies, PSU-132-AESR, exhaust air flow (datasheet Available to Order). Input 100 to 240 V at 12 A maximum per feed, IEC60320 C15 cord, with a 16 A fast-acting fuse in each supply. NO HELD IMAGE SHOWS THIS BUILD; the face drawn is ufispace/psu-132-ac as built for the S9300-32D, which orders the same 1300 W part family at the same 50.5 x 40.0 envelope.
configs.name: ac

configs.description: Four FAN-803816-HI exhaust fans and two PSU-132-DESR 1300 W DC supplies, front-to-back, with all eighty-two ports empty. The DC build is what the vendor's own rear render shows seated - the two-post screw terminal block behind its hinged cover - so this is read rather than chosen. No orderable chassis part number appears in any held document.
configs.name: base

configs.description: Dual 1300 W DC supplies, PSU-132-DESR, exhaust air flow (datasheet Available to Order). Input -40 to -75 V at 40 A maximum per feed, with a 60 A fast-acting fuse in each supply.
configs.name: dc

gaps.note: The white lozenge on each green band carries two dark glyph clusters - one on the up-triangle, one on the down-triangle - and neither source resolves them. Both images are the same raster at about 3.4 px/mm here, so a 1.5 mm numeral is five pixels. THE PRINTING IS THERE: the control is the crimson fabric band 25 mm to the right and the yellow SFP28 bands to the left, the same glyph size on grounds of the same darkness in the same crop, and both resolve cleanly. So this is an unresolved reading, not a blank area. The numerals drawn - 64/65, 66/67, 68/69, 70/71, 72/73, 74/75 - are the HIG port table's own range assigned in the order Figure 8 itself calls the shells out, so the VALUES are sourced even though the glyphs were not read. What is genuinely open is only their exact size and placement inside the lozenge.

gaps.note: The green band under the lower QSFP28 row ends at x 337.2, so ports 74 and 75 have their eight lane lamps and their number lozenge printed on bare panel while the other five pairs have them on green. The band above the upper row runs the full width across all three shells. Measured independently in both images and they agree - guide figure 291.26-337.23, product render 291.19-336.75 - which is why it is drawn rather than tidied to match the top band. Recorded as sources-disagree because the two sources agree with each other and disagree with the device's own symmetry everywhere else on this faceplate; a photograph of a real unit would settle whether the metal is really printed this way or whether both renders inherit one artwork slip.

gaps.note: HIG Figure 8 draws FIVE system lamps with a five-line plaque and the guide's own Front Panel LED table documents five - SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1, each with its own state list. The five system lamps and the two FRU lamps do carry the guide's real states.

The two symbols clearly name the RJ45 and the USB port; what the triangle pair names is not stated anywhere. On every other band of this faceplate that glyph pair marks the upper and lower port of a stack, so it is drawn attached to the two RJ45s on that reading - which is a reading, not a transcription, and it is recorded here rather than asserted in provenance as fact.

The underside is not shown in any image held at all; the bottom face carries only a compliance label at an estimated position, and nothing else is invented for it.

provenance.chassis: datasheet and HIG agree exactly - '2RU, 436 x 609.6 x 87.7 mm or 17.17" x 24" x 3.45"', 'Weight: 15.54 kg (Without FRU)'. 436 IS THE BODY, not a rack face: the HIG's Space Clearance paragraph says so in as many words - 'the S9701-82DC chassis width is 17.16 inches (43.6cm) and is shipped with an adjustable mounting rail kit suited for standard 19 inch (48.3cm) wide racks' - and Figure 8 draws the ear tabs standing proud of the full-height body. The 609.6 mm depth is likewise the body 'without the field replaceable units (FRUs)'; the HIG adds that the fan FRU handle projects 1.2 in (29 mm) and the PSU handle 1.1 in (27 mm) beyond it. Those projections are recorded here and not added to the depth.
provenance.front-layout: HIG Figure 8 at 8.940 / 8.917 px/mm, with the feature positions the figure hides behind seated transceivers taken from the front product render at 3.204 px/mm (see port-leds). Left to right: the timing block (GNSS SMA, 10MHz SMB, 1PPS SMB across the top, ToD RJ45 and the two SFP+ management ports below them, then the reset pinhole, the mgmt RJ45 / USB 3.0 / console RJ45 stack, the five system lamps and the micro-USB console); then four SFP28 shells over four more, each 58.50 x 27.25 mm on a 61.63 mm pitch from x 44.63; then three QSFP28 shells over three, 21.0 wide on a 23.65 mm pitch from x 291.04; then three QSFP-DD fabric shells, 20.0 wide on a 23.66 mm pitch from x 361.06, with the two-digit beacon display above them.
provenance.gate-1: THREE FIGURES WERE CHECKED AND ALL THREE PASS. (1) HIG Figure 8, the port overview (fig-0015, re-rendered from the PDF at 600 dpi): body 3898 x 782 px against the stated 436 x 87.7 mm, aspect 4.985 against a true 4.9715 - 0.27 % out - so it is orthographic and reads at 8.940 px/mm across and 8.917 down. Two small ear tabs stand outside the body at px 763-779 and 4678-4698 (1.9 mm each side); they are the mounting hardware and are not drawn. (2) The front product render (1397 x 281 px for the same body) gives 4.971 against 4.9715, 0.02 % out, at 3.204 px/mm. (3) The rear render (1298 x 262) gives 4.954, 0.35 % out, at 2.977 px/mm. (4) The HIG's top elevation in Figure 4 measures 726 x 1023 px against 436 x 609.6, aspect 0.7097 against 0.7152, 0.77 % out, at 1.665 / 1.678 px/mm. The two front sources are 8.9 and 3.2 px/mm, so a coordinate quoted here to a hundredth is good to about a tenth of a millimetre on the guide figure and about three tenths on the render, NOT to the hundredth the arithmetic prints.

provenance.panel-decor: photo-measured, and the bands are drawn where they stop rather than where symmetry would put them. Hexagonal vent perforation fills x 69.2-406.2 above the yellow band, x 46.1-362 below it, and the whole right-hand region x 362-432 except where the beacon tile, the crimson band and the fabric shells sit; two small honeycomb patches sit in the left block at (5.4, 15.7) and (5.4, 53.8). Band colours are the modal pixel of each band in the front render: yellow #e5cd2b, green #5b7744, crimson #ac505d, panel #464646, shells and bezels #b9b9b9, the SMA/SMB nuts #d0c02d. THE BOTTOM GREEN BAND STOPS AFTER THE SECOND SHELL. It runs x 291.0-337.2, so the lamps and the lozenge of the third pair (ports 74/75) sit on bare panel while every other lane-lamp group in the device sits on a coloured ground. That asymmetry is drawn because BOTH images show it - the guide figure and the product render, measured independently at 337.23 and 336.75 - and the top green band in the same two images runs the full 291.0-360.5 across all three shells. It looks like an artwork slip and it may be one, but it is what the vendor draws twice, so it is not tidied; see the green-band-stop gap.
provenance.part-numbers: The datasheet's Available to Order block names PSU-132-DESR (1300 W DC, exhaust), PSU-132-AESR (1300 W AC, exhaust) and FAN-803816-HI (exhaust). The fan is an exact match for library ufispace/fan-803816-hi, built from the S9600-28DX - the same 2RU 436 x 87.7 chassis family - and reused unchanged. THE SUPPLIES ARE NOT AN EXACT MATCH: library ufispace/psu-132-ac and -dc were drawn for the S9300-32D, which orders PSU-132-AISB1 and PSU-132-DISB1 - the INTAKE variants of the same 1300 W part, at the same 50.5 x 40.0 face this guide's own component table states. The rear render's DC supply matches ufispace/psu-132-dc's face feature for feature (silver face, red release latch on the left, two-post screw terminal block under a hinged cover, square-hole vent grid, wire bail on the right, status lamp lower left), so the component is reused with its model attribute overridden per configuration and the airflow difference filed rather than hidden. See the psu-airflow-variant gap. The guide's component table also gives the fan as 81 x 113 x 81.5 mm where the S9600-28DX guide the component was built from says 80 x 113 x 81.5. One millimetre, two guides, same part number; the component's 80 is kept and the disagreement is in the fan-face-width gap.
provenance.port-leds: photo-measured from the front product render, because HIG Figure 8 draws the shells with transceivers seated and every per-port lamp is hidden behind a module face. SFP28: one green up-triangle and one green down-triangle per column on the silver inter-row strip, at the column centre -1.87 and +1.87 mm and on the strip centreline (28.70 in the upper shell row, 58.90 in the lower) - 128 lamps, two per column, counted across all eight shells. They are 3.74 mm apart, so common/led-arrow (3.6 mm wide) would have to touch and common/led-arrow-sm (2.25) is used: the right pitch in a smaller shape, the same compromise the S9620-54DC records. QSFP28: four round lamps per port, in two rows of four on the coloured band outside the shell - the upper row for the even port, the lower for the odd - at a 3.99 mm pitch starting 4.0 mm inside the shell's left edge, which is ufispace/lane-led-quad's own 3.94 mm to 1.3 %. Rows 3.24 mm apart. QSFP-DD: TWO lamps per shell, one per port, on the crimson band at shell x +7.9 and +12.1 mm - not four and not eight. That is measured in both images and is why no lane strip is used here. WHAT THE LAMPS MEAN IS NOT PUBLISHED. The HIG's section 10 tables SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0 and PS1, the PSU FRU lamp, the fan FRU lamp and the management RJ45's left/right pair, and says nothing about any port lamp, so every port lamp keeps its component's plain off/on default. See the port-led-semantics gap.
provenance.port-numbers: TRANSCRIBED, NOT RECONSTRUCTED. The HIG's Port Overview table gives the three ranges - '0 ~ 63 SFP28 1/10/25G', '64 ~ 75 QSFP28 40/100G', '0 ~ 5 QSFP-DD 400G' - and Figure 8 prints the individual numerals large enough to read at 600 dpi: the yellow band above each SFP28 shell carries 'N (up-triangle)(down-triangle) N+1' per column, even on the top row and odd on the bottom, 0-31 across the upper shell row and 32-63 across the lower; the crimson fabric band prints '0 (up) o o (down) 1', '2 ... 3', '4 ... 5'. The fabric ports therefore have their OWN numbering space starting at 0, which is the vendor's, not an editorial choice. THE QSFP28 NUMERALS ARE THE ONE SET THAT IS NOT LEGIBLE. Each green band carries a white lozenge - an up-triangle over a down-triangle - with two dark glyph clusters inside it, and at 3.4 px/mm (both images are the same raster resolution here) the digits will not separate. That printing EXISTS is a positive reading, not a guess: the same crop resolves the neighbouring crimson band's numerals and the yellow band's, which are the same glyph size on the same darkness of ground. The values 64/65 ... 74/75 come from the HIG's port table and from Figure 8's own callout numbering of those very shells, so they are drawn; that the GLYPHS were not read is recorded in the qsfp28-numeral-glyphs gap.
provenance.power: THREE FIGURES, THREE SCOPES, ALL THE VENDOR'S OWN. The datasheet gives 'Typical Power: 311 Watts (no transceiver)' - the vendor states the scope, so power-envelope is bare. The HIG's Connecting Power section gives a maximum twice, once per input type: 'The maximum system power consumption is 904 watts' under DC Version and '900 watts' under AC Version. Those are not a disagreement, they are the same measure at two scopes; 904 is carried as power-max-w because it is the higher and it matches the base configuration's DC build, and the AC figure is recorded here. Neither maximum is qualified by ambient or by optics loading anywhere in the guide, and that silence is the vendor's. A FOURTH NUMBER IN THE SAME GUIDE IS NOT A POWER FIGURE AT ALL: 'a reserve of at least 1300 watts on each power circuit' is the provisioning instruction for a 1+1 feed and equals one supply's nameplate, not the box's draw. Inputs are the datasheet's and the guide's check list agrees: 100-240 V 12 A AC max, -40 to -75 V 40 A DC max, per feed, x2. Each supply is 1300 W from its ordering line. The DC supply carries a built-in 60 A fast-acting fuse and the AC a 16 A one (HIG). THE FANS PUBLISH NO DRAW. Both documents were searched for 'W', 'Watt' and 'power': every hit is one of the three system figures, the 1300 W reserve, or a PSU ordering line. The L27/L29 warning therefore stands and the modelled module total is a floor.

provenance.rear-layout: photo-measured from the rear product render at 2.977 px/mm, corroborated by the rear elevation in HIG Figure 4. Four fan bays on an 85.1 mm pitch from x 2.0, each seating ufispace/fan-803816-hi at its documented 80 x 81.5 mm face, vertically centred at y 3.1: the four red release tabs measure x 4.03, 89.01, 174.33 and 259.65 (deltas 84.98, 85.32, 85.32) and the four red loop handles 33.9, 118.9, 203.7, 288.7 (deltas 85.0, 84.8, 85.0), and the last fan's right edge lands on the measured bay seam at 337.5. THE RENDER SHOWS THE DC BUILD, with the two-post screw terminal block behind its hinged cover, which is what fixes the base configuration; the AC build is not photographed anywhere held.
provenance.sfp-layout: THE PITCH IS TAKEN FROM THE PER-PORT ARROW LAMPS, which repeat once per port column, NOT from the filled module faces Figure 8 draws. In the front render the eight green arrow pairs of shell 1 sit at 50.56/54.30, 64.92/68.66, 79.12/83.02 and 93.47/97.07 mm; their midpoints are 52.43, 66.79, 81.07, 95.27, a pitch of 14.36, 14.28 and 14.20 - mean 14.28 against the SFF-8433 B04 ganged basic of 14.25, 0.2 % apart. The standard 14.25 is therefore used, anchored 0.75 mm inside each measured shell edge, which puts column 1 of shell 1 at 52.50 against the measured 52.43 and column 4 at 95.25 against 95.27 - the run closes on itself across the shell to 0.02 mm. (Measuring the same block off Figure 8's white column separators instead gives 14.47, 1.5 % high, which is the module-face error the skill warns about; it is recorded here so the next reader can see which reading was rejected and why.) ROW PITCH IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. Both sources put the four aperture centrelines at 20.57, 36.22, 50.95 and 66.64 mm (guide 20.53/36.23/51.03/66.79, render 20.60/36.20/50.87/66.48). That is 15.65 mm belly-to-belly INSIDE a shell and 14.73 between shells - the intra-shell figure is 4.3 % wider than SFF-8433's 15.00, and two independent images agreeing to 0.3 mm is what says it is the hardware and not the drawing, so the measured centres are used and the standard is not imposed. The standard 14.25 x 10.4 aperture is used at those centres; the black area Figure 8 draws inside each cage is 8.1 mm tall, which is the visible opening inside the bezel lip and not a smaller cage.

provenance.timing-and-mgmt: HIG Figure 8, with the legends read at 600 dpi. THE SMB ASSIGNMENT IS PRINTED AND WAS READ, not conventioned: 'GNSS ANT' beside the large gold nut at (21.98, 7.57), 10.18 mm across; '10MHZ' beside the 7.94 mm nut at (39.54, 7.57); '1PPS' beside the 7.94 mm nut at (56.99, 7.40). The SMA is the larger of the three, which is what the datasheet's one SMA and two SMB implies, and the guide's own Cable Connections sections name all three ports by those legends. Construction follows the S9311-64D and S9610-36D: a gold decor disc for the knurled nut with the registry bore (std/sma 6.35, std/smb 4.83) on top. 'TOD' labels the RJ45 at x 7.16-22.59, y 28.37-41.61 - a 15.44 x 13.23 mm bright bezel, which std/rj45's 16.0 x 14.0 registry aperture fits to half a millimetre. The two 10G SFP+ management ports are a stacked pair in one 15.10 x 25.90 shell at (26.73, 15.59), apertures centred (34.23, 20.81) and (34.23, 36.45) - a 15.64 mm row pitch, the same as the traffic shells - legended '0 (up)(down) 1' above and carrying the same green arrow pair between the cages. The mgmt RJ45, the USB 3.0 Type-A and the console RJ45 are a vertical stack in one 15.77 x 31.63 shell at (21.92, 49.23); their apertures measure y 49.79-59.89, 62.1-67.7 and 70.43-80.63. The micro-USB console sits below at (9.51, 79.96), 8.39 x 2.36. BOTH CONSOLES ARE LETTERED IOIOI, which is what the guide's Initial System Setup section says: 'The console can be connected either with the RJ45 port or the micro USB port, both labelled IOIO'. The out-of-band RJ45 carries the two integrated lamps the guide's Management port LED table documents - a left 1G link/activity lamp and a right 10M/100M one - photo-measured at (24.56, 51.42) and (35.07, 51.48); std/rj45 draws the aperture and not those lamps, so they are placed on top of it, which is why they overlap its box. The recessed reset pinhole is at (14.88, 46.65) with RESET printed under it.
provenance.views: Six views, all with drawn content. TOP is measured, not estimated: HIG Figure 4's top elevation passes Gate 1 at 0.77 % and gives five long rounded stiffening ribs 400.3 mm wide from x 18.0, at y 118.6, 213.9, 309.9, 405.8 and 501.1 on a 95.6 mm pitch, each about 23 mm across. Y = 0 IS THE REAR on that face, per the house convention and per the figure itself, which prints the fan and supply handles at the top of the frame and the front timing jacks at the bottom. BOTTOM mirrors left and right and carries only a compliance label at an ESTIMATED position; no image held shows the underside. LEFT (x = 0 is the REAR) and RIGHT (x = 0 is the FRONT) each carry the five rail attachment pins the guide counts - 'The chassis has 5 attachment pins on each side, for a total of 10 pins' - and the single M4 inner-rail locking screw the guide says sits at the front. THE COUNT IS SOURCED AND EVERY POSITION IS ESTIMATED: no figure dimensions them and the side is not photographed straight on. Both side faces carry only symmetric content, so the depth-axis conventions are stated here rather than exposed by an asymmetric feature.
